purpose: Read-only diagnosis of a different question from global Brier: whether the retained fixed-parent state value ranks existing deterministic card successors. E169/E170 remain rejected by their original prediction gate. This does not reopen that gate or authorize policy deployment.
population: All observed branching normal-monster/elite reward states whose parent action is card/bowl/skip and whose complete legal card/bowl/skip menu has recorded nonterminal successors; require all1536 admitted initial floor1 card roots. Family-excluding source models only. Later states remain correlated branches, not independent natural runs.
inputs: Recorded successor public state, using the exact source predictor mask. Require changed retained coordinates to belong only to deterministic acquisition resources/cards/relic counters or the reward-to-map screen. Join every initial root to the old public observation, full descriptor menu and parent action. No seed or RNG in the predictor.
choice: Canonical independent NumPy sigmoid score, maximum first, parent then lower action index for exact ties. Keep parent if the best advantage is at most1e-6. Resolve choice before loading successor outcome labels. No margin or checkpoint sweep.
labels: Parent_value of the actual recorded successor. Verify parent successor label matches parent_value of the current state; report all initial families including unchanged or tied outcomes. No observed_best/terminal-hindsight maximization as a prediction.
decision: This diagnostic ends with signed gains/losses and fit-excluded initial/later counts. No training or natural-game entry is provided. Positive diagnostic evidence would still require a separately declared live public-effect interface and policy experiment; failure closes use of this frozen predictor for card scoring.
limits: These old families have informed previous designs; no result is fresh unseen acceptance or a deployed action policy.
